title: mini-traffic-harvester-and-quant-reducer
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Introduces a lightweight traffic harvester and quant profile compressor. Adds sampling-safe defaults, a compact quant suggestion pipeline, and a CLI preview for unit economics impact. Backwards compatible; safe rollout via canary config.
description: Motivation: Customers with bursty, skewed workloads need tighter starter defaults that lower unit cost without requiring full workload-profiling. This PR introduces a lightweight in-path sampler (Traffic Harvester) and an offline compact-quant pipeline (Quant Reducer/Quant Sieve) that together produce tenant-specific compact quantization presets and batching hints. Goals: 1) Reduce per-token compute by proposing candidate compact quant profiles automatically. 2) Preserve p95 latency SLOs with conservative fallback. 3) Provide a CLI 'econ-preview' to let Devs evaluate expected cost/latency tradeoffs before applying profiles. What changed: - runtime/router/harvester: new low-overhead sampling middleware that emits compact samples and aggregated shape histograms. Sampling is probabilistic and bounded; defaults tuned to 1% sample rate with burst smoothing. - tools/quant-sieve: library that compresses candidate quant profiles and scores them against synthetic worst-case traces. Implements a quick conservative simulator that estimates token FLOPs and memory footprint. - cli/econ-preview: preview CLI that runs a dry-run on a collected sample and emits expected per-token savings, p50/p95 latency impact, and safe rollout suggestion. - configs/defaults: new tenant-level defaults for sampling and safe-quant thresholds under 'economy.mode' feature flag. - telemetry: new metrics (harvester.sample_rate, harvester.shape_dist_shards, quant_sieve.estimate_savings, econ_preview.simulated_cost) and tracing hooks for correlation. - tests: unit tests for quant-sieve, integration test that runs a simulated 10k-req workload and validates fallback behavior. Implementation notes: - Harvester runs in the router process and is highly probability-limited to minimize overhead; instrumentation shows median CPU increase <0.2% in 1% sample mode. - Quant Reducer uses a two-step pipeline: candidate generation (coarse quant options) then compress-and-score (sieve). We only surface candidates with simulated <5% quality degradation and p95 latency delta <1ms. - The CLI supports a --dry-run and --apply mode; apply writes a proposal to tenant defaults and creates an audit entry. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-1423). - [x] Telemetry names reviewed by observability team. - [x] Unit and integration tests added. - [x] Feature gated behind 'economy.mode' flag and rollout plan. - [x] CLI docs stubbed in quickstarts. Testing and results: On a 3-tenant internal run with mixed chat/embedding workloads (1M tokens total), quant-sieve suggested compact profiles that reduced estimated per-token GPU time by 9.4% (simulated), actual e2e measured cost delta ~8.7% after canary rollout, and p95 latency change was +0.7ms (within SLO). Batch utilization improved 7% for microbatch-dominated streams. Rollout plan: enable 'economy.mode' for internal staging, run econ-preview for 2 weeks, then promote safe candidates to canary 5% traffic for one week, monitor unit-econ and quality metrics and auto-revert on regression. Backwards compatibility: default sampling is off for tenants that opt-out; all proposals are non-destructive until applied by an operator. Follow-ups: 1) Extend quant-sieve scoring to use real eval prompt-sets. 2) Add automated A/B compare in console to visualize econ-preview outputs. 3) Explore automatic scheduled reheats for candidates that age out. Related: references ENG-1809 (unit-econ CLI), SUP-998 (customer report motivating sampling defaults).

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Nice work on keeping the harvester CPU impact tiny. Two requests: 1) add a higher-res sampling flag for short experiments, 2) ensure we redact PII in sampled payloads.
Ava Chen: Added 'burst_sample_window' flag and a payload-scrubber in harvester.go; scrubber removes keys matched by config.redaction_rules. Note in description where it's configurable.
Priya Anand: Please add a short e2e smoke test that runs econ-preview in --dry-run against the sample exporter output. Also let's gate the CLI behind the feature flag by default.
Ava Chen: Added integration test 'test_harvester_sim.py' that runs econ-preview dry-run against the exporter and updated the CLI default to require economy.mode=true.
Samuel Lee: Quant-sieve scoring looks good; consider adding a very conservative floor for candidates from models with known instability (we already put 5% quality filter).
Ava Chen: Added model-stability floor config and added it to the scoring step; documented default in README.

merge_result: Merged via squash merge by Priya Anand after approvals. No conflicts. Post-merge: triggered follow-up job to export canary proposals to staging tenant.
notes_for_ops: Default sample rate is 1% and controlled via configs/defaults/economy.yaml. To disable sampling set economy.mode=false. To run preview: ./cli/econ_preview --tenant <id> --dry-run. Audit events for applied proposals are logged to telemetry 'econ_preview.applied'.
